titles.ja: 引き継ぎの完了条件を確認する

objectives_zh_TW: 用可觀察條件界定交接完成。
向接手者確認檔案、權限與驗收責任。
寫出含期限、例外與回覆要求的交接訊息。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 把自己的「做好了」換成接手者可以逐項檢查的條件；傳送檔案不等於對方已驗收。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional design team, Nora sends a product leaflet to the sales coordinator, Amir, with the message, 'All done.' Amir assumes that the leaflet can go to the printer. Nora means only that the layout is ready for review. Their manager asks them to agree on acceptance criteria before transferring responsibility. Nora will provide the editable source file, a printable draft, and a list of unresolved comments. Amir will check that every link works and that the leaflet uses the approved prices. He will also confirm that he can open the source file. If a check fails, he will return the checklist with a specific issue rather than silently repairing it. The marketing lead, not Amir, will approve the final version for printing. Their handoff note records these responsibilities and asks Amir to acknowledge acceptance. Sending a file now starts a review; it does not automatically authorize publication.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words drafting the handoff note. Include deliverables, acceptance checks, final approval authority, and what happens if a check fails.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞的交接訊息，包含交付項目、驗收檢查、最終核准權限，以及未通過檢查的處理方式。
practice.sample_answer_en: Hi Amir, the leaflet layout is ready for your review. I have included the editable source file, printable draft, and unresolved comments. Before accepting the handoff, please check that you can open the source file, all links work, and the approved prices appear. If anything fails, please return the checklist with the relevant page and issue so I can correct it. Your acceptance confirms that the handoff meets these conditions; it does not approve printing. The marketing lead will approve the final version separately. Could you acknowledge receipt and confirm when you can complete the checks? I will remain responsible for the draft until you accept the handoff.

questions.prompt_en: Why do Nora and Amir interpret the first message differently?
questions.answer_en: Nora means the layout is ready for review, while Amir thinks the leaflet is approved for printing.

questions.prompt_en: How does the checklist change responsibility transfer?
questions.answer_en: Amir checks specific conditions and acknowledges acceptance; responsibility no longer transfers merely because Nora sends a file.

questions.prompt_en: Would a working source file alone justify printing? Give a reason.
questions.answer_en: No. Other checks remain, and only the marketing lead can approve the final version for printing.

titles.ja: 作業の依存関係と影響を説明する

objectives_zh_TW: 清楚指出工作開始所需的前置資料。
把延遲與後續交付影響連結。
提出有條件的替代流程而不假裝已獲批准。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 寫出「缺什麼→哪項工作受影響→可怎麼調整」；不要只說被某個部門卡住。

practice.reading_en: At a fictional service company, Elena is preparing a guide for new support staff. The product team has not yet approved its list of service features. Elena can write the welcome section, but she cannot verify the guide's examples without the approved list. Her first status message says that the product team is blocking training. She rewrites it to explain the dependency instead of assigning blame. The examples require confirmed feature descriptions; if approval arrives after Thursday, the planned review will move to the following week. Elena proposes drafting the general introduction in parallel. She clearly labels the feature examples as pending and asks the training manager to approve this partial approach. The product team agrees to provide an update on Thursday, but does not promise final approval that day. The revised message distinguishes a status update from a delivery commitment and gives colleagues a useful choice while the missing input is resolved.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words updating the training manager. Explain the missing input, its effect, the proposed parallel work, and the decision you need.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞向訓練主管更新狀況，說明缺少的前置資料、影響、可並行工作與需要的決定。
practice.sample_answer_en: The guide's examples depend on the approved feature list, which is still under review. Without it, I cannot confirm that the examples accurately describe the service. If approval arrives after Thursday, the guide review will need to move to next week. I propose drafting the general introduction now and leaving the feature examples clearly marked as pending. This would let us make progress without presenting unapproved information as final. Please confirm whether you approve that partial approach. The product team has promised a Thursday status update, not final approval on Thursday. After that update, I will revise the schedule and explain whether the original review date remains possible.

questions.prompt_en: Which part of the guide can Elena draft before feature approval?
questions.answer_en: She can draft the general introduction or welcome section.

questions.prompt_en: Why is the revised status message more useful than the first?
questions.answer_en: It identifies the required input, the effect of late approval, and a parallel work option instead of assigning blame.

questions.prompt_en: Can the manager assume that the feature list will be approved on Thursday? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. The product team has promised only a status update on Thursday, not final approval.

titles.ja: リスクと選択肢を早めに伝える

objectives_zh_TW: 區分風險、已發生問題與確定結果。
用具體觀察支持風險提醒。
提供替代方案並設定決策時點。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 風險訊息要回答「為何現在要注意」；同時附上可行選項與何時必須決定。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional events agency, Daniel is coordinating a small product launch. The venue has not confirmed when presenters can enter for rehearsal. Nothing has failed yet, but the missing confirmation creates a risk: the team may have no chance to test the room's presentation equipment before the event. Daniel alerts his manager while alternatives are still available. A remote rehearsal would help speakers practice their transitions, but it would not test the venue equipment. An earlier site visit could address that gap, although the venue must agree and a coordinator would need to attend. Daniel asks the manager to choose a backup by Wednesday so there is time to arrange it. He also requests a fresh venue update that morning. His message does not claim that the launch will definitely be delayed. It explains the warning sign, the possible consequence, and the limitations of each response before a preventable problem becomes urgent.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words raising the rehearsal risk. Include the observed warning sign, possible impact, two options with limitations, and a decision deadline.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞提出彩排風險，包含警訊、可能影響、兩項選擇及限制，與決策期限。
practice.sample_answer_en: The venue has not confirmed rehearsal access, so we may be unable to test the room equipment before the launch. This is a risk rather than a confirmed delay. We could rehearse remotely to practice speaker transitions, but that would leave the equipment untested. Alternatively, we could request an earlier site visit, subject to venue approval and a coordinator being available. I will ask the venue for another update on Wednesday morning. Please choose a backup by Wednesday so we can arrange it in time. If access is confirmed before then, I will check whether the original rehearsal still covers both speaker practice and equipment testing.

questions.prompt_en: What observation leads Daniel to raise a risk?
questions.answer_en: The venue has not confirmed access for rehearsal.

questions.prompt_en: Why are remote rehearsal and an earlier site visit not equivalent?
questions.answer_en: Remote rehearsal can test speaker transitions but not the room equipment; a site visit can address equipment testing but requires venue approval and staff availability.

questions.prompt_en: Why is Daniel justified in contacting his manager before anything fails?
questions.answer_en: A decision is needed by Wednesday to arrange a backup, so early notice preserves workable options.

objectives_zh_TW: 用交付影響表達容量限制。
把優先順序轉成可決定的取捨。

episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 不要同時承諾互相衝突的期限；把可選路徑與各自代價寫清楚。

practice.reading_en: At a fictional consulting office, Maya is reviewing the monthly report when her manager requests an urgent proposal. Both documents need the same afternoon review slot. Maya could say yes to both and work without a clear plan, but that would hide the conflict until a deadline is missed. Instead, she presents two paths. She can prioritize the proposal if the report deadline moves to the following morning. Alternatively, another qualified reviewer could handle the report while she finishes the proposal. She explains that an unreviewed report is not a useful third option because the report goes directly to the planning meeting. The manager decides that the proposal matters most this week and authorizes the later report. Maya records the new deadline and tells the planning coordinator, who adjusts the meeting materials. Her response protects the important outcome without treating every request as equally urgent or assuming permission to move someone else's deadline.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words replying to the urgent proposal request. Explain the conflict, offer two realistic options, request a priority decision, and describe follow-up.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞回覆緊急提案要求，說明衝突、兩個可行方案、需要的優先決定與後續通知。
practice.sample_answer_en: I can review the urgent proposal this afternoon, but it needs the same review time as the monthly report. If the proposal takes priority, I will need approval to deliver the report tomorrow morning. A second option is to assign another qualified reviewer to the report so both original deadlines can remain. Sending the report without review would create a problem for the planning meeting, so I do not recommend that approach. Which outcome should take priority this week? Once you choose an option, I will confirm the schedule in writing and notify the planning coordinator and any other colleagues affected by the revised deadline.

titles.ja: 出来事を時系列で報告する

objectives_zh_TW: 按順序區分發現、確認與處理。
避免把事件時間先後誤寫成因果。
在簡報中標明影響範圍與尚待查證事項。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 事件摘要先寫可核對的觀察；「在更新之後」不等於「由更新造成」。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional shared office, reception staff report that the booking calendar is unavailable on Tuesday morning. The office coordinator confirms that the problem affects reception and the meeting room desk. Existing printed schedules remain available, so staff can still check bookings already recorded. New requests go onto a temporary form approved for this fictional exercise. The coordinator's incident summary orders the known events: staff reported the issue, the coordinator confirmed its scope, and reception began recording new requests separately. A colleague mentions a calendar update from the previous evening. The coordinator records this as background, not as a confirmed cause. The service team has not yet established why access failed. The summary promises another update after the service team responds and names the coordinator as the communication owner. It avoids repair instructions, speculation about individual mistakes, and a recovery time that nobody has verified. Readers can distinguish observed facts from unanswered questions.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words giving a factual incident update. Include the event sequence, known impact, temporary handling, uncertainty about cause, and the next update.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞的事實性事件更新，包含事件順序、已知影響、暫時處理、原因不確定性與下次更新。
practice.sample_answer_en: Reception reported that the booking calendar was unavailable on Tuesday morning. The coordinator then confirmed that reception and the meeting room desk were affected. Existing printed schedules remain available for checking previously recorded bookings. Reception is recording new requests on the approved temporary form used in this exercise. A calendar update took place yesterday evening, but we have not established that it caused the access problem. The service team is reviewing the cause, and no recovery time has been confirmed. I will coordinate communication and share another confirmed update after the service team responds. Please keep observations separate from possible explanations when adding information to the incident record.

questions.prompt_en: Which booking information remains available?
questions.answer_en: Existing printed schedules remain available for bookings already recorded.

questions.prompt_en: Why does the coordinator mention the previous update only as background?
questions.answer_en: The timing is known, but the service team has not established a causal connection to the access problem.

questions.prompt_en: Would promising immediate recovery be supported by the summary? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. The cause and recovery time are unverified, and the coordinator promises only a confirmed update after the service team responds.

titles.ja: 症状と原因の仮説を区別する

objectives_zh_TW: 用觀察陳述問題現象。
將可能原因標記為待驗證假說。
選擇能區分競爭解釋的下一步證據。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 先問哪個觀察能區分兩種解釋，避免把第一個想到的原因寫成定論。

practice.reading_en: At a fictional training center, several registration forms arrive without department names. The administrator initially suggests that staff are ignoring instructions. A colleague separates the observation from that explanation: the names are missing, but nobody has established why. One hypothesis is that the department label is unclear. Another is that staff are using an older form without that field. The team decides to compare submitted form versions and ask volunteers to explain how they interpreted the current label. If missing names occur mainly on the older form, replacing outdated copies may help. If people using the current form misunderstand the label, a wording change may be needed. Both explanations could also contribute. The administrator records each hypothesis and the evidence that would support it. The team has not yet selected a final fix. This approach avoids blaming people before checking the materials and makes the next information request more focused.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words proposing an investigation note. Separate the observed problem from two possible causes and explain which evidence would distinguish them.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞的調查建議，區分問題現象與兩個可能原因，說明能區分它們的證據。
practice.sample_answer_en: The observed problem is that several registration forms lack department names. We should not conclude that staff ignored instructions without checking other explanations. One possibility is that the current field label is unclear. Another is that some people received an older form without the field. I suggest comparing the submitted versions first and then asking volunteers how they understood the current label. Missing names mainly on old forms would support replacing outdated copies. Misunderstanding among users of the current form would support revising the wording. Both causes may contribute, so the evidence could justify more than one change. We should record our findings before choosing a final response.

questions.prompt_en: How do the proposed checks relate to the two hypotheses?

questions.prompt_en: Would evidence for one hypothesis automatically rule out the other? Give a reason.
questions.answer_en: No. The reading explicitly allows both outdated forms and unclear wording to contribute to the missing names.

episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 把「不夠細心」改成某次具體行為、造成的影響及下一次可採取的做法。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional operations team, Luis asks Priya to review his handover notes. He wants to know whether the next action is clear, rather than asking whether she likes his writing. Priya identifies a specific example: yesterday's note included a deadline but did not name an owner for the supplier query. Both teams waited for the other to answer, so the query remained open. Priya avoids calling Luis careless. She explains the behavior, its effect, and a possible adjustment: confirm an owner before sending the next note. Luis explains that the receiving team had not accepted responsibility when he wrote it. Together they add a pending-owner label and a request for confirmation instead of assigning someone without agreement. They will review the next handover to see whether the action is clearer. objectives_zh_TW: 承認不同方案背後的合理需求。
先確認共同評估標準再比較。

episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 先找雙方都接受的判斷標準；對方案的喜好不是證據。

practice.reading_en: At a fictional publishing office, the editorial and finance teams disagree about a purchase request form. Editors want fewer questions so they can submit requests quickly. Finance staff want enough context to review unusual purchases without repeated messages. Rather than voting on the most popular design, they agree on shared criteria: reasonable completion effort and enough information for a decision. They compare a short version with a longer version using the same fictional sample requests. The short form may save writing time but create more follow-up questions. The longer form may prevent those questions but repeat information already held elsewhere. Neither effect has been measured yet. The teams plan a small trial and agree to record both completion effort and requests for clarification. They will also remove fields that duplicate existing records. The disagreement becomes a testable design question, while the shared criteria make it harder for either team to ignore the other's work.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words proposing a way to resolve the form disagreement. Include shared criteria, both tradeoffs, a fair comparison, and the later decision.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞提出表單分歧的處理方法，包含共同標準、雙方取捨、公平比較與後續決策。
practice.sample_answer_en: Both teams need a form that is manageable to complete and useful for reviewing purchases. I suggest using those two criteria before choosing a design. A short form may reduce writing but increase follow-up questions; a longer form may provide context while repeating information we already hold. Let us test both versions with the same fictional sample requests and record completion effort as well as clarification requests. We should also identify fields that duplicate existing records. After the trial, we can compare the results and revise either version if necessary. This gives us a shared basis for deciding without treating one team's preference as proof that its design works better.

questions.prompt_en: Would choosing the shorter form immediately be evidence-based? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. Its possible time savings and follow-up costs have not been measured; the planned trial is meant to test them.

practice.reading_en: In a fictional coworking business, the community team is revising its visitor guide. The facilities team knows which entrance delivery staff should use, but it has not been involved in writing the guide. Community coordinator Asha therefore adds context to her request instead of sending an unexplained document and asking for approval. She asks facilities to confirm the approved delivery entrance and the contact point listed beside it. The information is needed before Friday's guide review. Asha explains that she will remain responsible for editing the document; facilities is being asked only to verify the stated facts. She includes the relevant paragraph rather than expecting colleagues to search the whole guide. She also asks them to suggest another contact or a workable date if the deadline is difficult. The message does not assume that a request automatically becomes someone else's commitment. It provides enough detail for the receiving team to assess the work and reply usefully.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words requesting a factual check from facilities. Explain the purpose, exact input, deadline, responsibility boundary, and an alternative if timing is difficult.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞請設施團隊核對事實，交代目的、具體輸入、期限、責任界線與時間難配合時的替代方式。
practice.sample_answer_en: Hello Facilities Team, we are revising the visitor guide before its Friday review. Could you check the attached paragraph and confirm the approved delivery entrance and the contact point listed beside it? Your knowledge will help us avoid directing delivery staff to the wrong place. This is a request to verify those facts, not to write or approve the entire guide. I will remain responsible for editing the document and incorporating your corrections. Please let me know whether you can provide the check before Friday's review. If that timing is difficult, could you suggest another suitable contact or a date that would be workable for your team?

questions.prompt_en: What exactly does Asha ask facilities to verify?
questions.answer_en: The approved delivery entrance and the contact point listed beside it.

questions.prompt_en: Why does she include only the relevant paragraph?
questions.answer_en: It lets facilities assess the requested factual check without searching the whole guide.

questions.prompt_en: Which feature shows that Asha is not assuming an automatic commitment?
questions.answer_en: She asks for a different contact or workable date if the deadline is difficult, allowing the team to respond to the request.

practice.reading_en: At a fictional communications agency, a client approves a digital brochure for an upcoming launch. Later, the client asks for printed copies as well and calls this a small format change. Project lead Ben explains the additional work without dismissing the request. Printed copies require a proof review, confirmed quantities, and a supplier deadline. These steps were not included in the agreed digital package. Ben offers two options: release the digital brochure on the original date and arrange printing afterward, or revise the schedule so both versions arrive together. He does not invent a printing date before checking supplier availability. The client chooses the staged delivery, subject to reviewing a separate printing estimate. Ben records the new scope and identifies what still needs approval. The team continues the digital work but does not ask the printer to start yet. Clear scope communication preserves a useful deadline while keeping added work and unresolved decisions visible.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words responding to the printing request. Identify the added scope, schedule effects, two delivery options, and approval needed before printing starts.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞回覆印製要求，指出新增範圍、時程影響、兩種交付方式及開印前需要的核准。
practice.sample_answer_en: We can explore printed copies, but they add work beyond the agreed digital brochure. Printing requires a proof review, confirmed quantities, and a supplier deadline. One option is to release the digital version on the original launch date and arrange printing afterward. The other is to revise the schedule so both versions arrive together. I will need to check supplier availability before confirming a printing date. If you prefer staged delivery, we can continue the digital work while preparing a separate printing estimate. Please approve the revised scope and estimate before we ask the printer to start. This will keep the additional work and remaining decisions clear.

practice.reading_en: In a fictional workshop supplier, a package of printed exercises fails to arrive before a customer's session. Support representative Leila confirms the missed delivery and acknowledges that the group could not complete its planned activities. She does not argue that the materials may still be useful later. Under the invented rules of this training scenario, Leila may send digital materials and request a replacement shipment, but a supervisor must approve refunds. She offers to send the digital version today and confirm the replacement delivery separately after checking availability. She also offers to request a refund review without promising its result. The customer prefers the digital materials immediately and asks for the review. Leila records both requests and promises an update tomorrow even if the review remains pending. Her plan gives the customer a definite next contact while keeping delivery dates and compensation decisions within the information and authority she actually has.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words responding to the customer. Acknowledge the impact, offer immediate help, explain the refund limit, and commit to a realistic update.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞回覆客戶，承認影響、提供即時協助、說明退款權限限制，並承諾可達成的更新。
practice.sample_answer_en: I am sorry the printed exercises did not arrive before your workshop. I understand that your group could not complete the activities you had planned. I can send the digital materials today so you have access to them immediately. I can also request a replacement shipment and confirm its delivery separately after checking availability. Under the rules of this training scenario, a supervisor must approve refunds, so I can request a review but cannot promise its outcome. I have recorded your request for that review. I will update you tomorrow even if a decision is still pending, and I will clearly separate confirmed arrangements from items awaiting approval.

questions.prompt_en: What immediate help can Leila provide?
questions.answer_en: She can send the digital materials today.

questions.prompt_en: Why does she discuss the replacement delivery separately?
questions.answer_en: Its availability and delivery timing still need confirmation, so she cannot responsibly promise a date yet.

questions.prompt_en: Does tomorrow's update guarantee a refund decision? Give evidence.
questions.answer_en: No. Leila promises to update the customer even if the supervisor's review is still pending.

titles.ja: プロジェクト立て直しの要点をまとめる

objectives_zh_TW: 整合事實、依賴、風險與範圍取捨。
讓補救計畫包含已確認責任與驗收條件。

episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 整合複習：讓讀者找到目前事實、選項取捨、誰做什麼、何時檢查與哪一項還沒批准。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional recruitment project, a welcome pack is running late because its approved contact list arrived after the planned editing slot. Project lead Owen writes a recovery brief that separates confirmed facts from open decisions. The essential guide is drafted, but optional building maps still require review. He proposes releasing the guide first and sending the maps later. This protects the start date while creating a separate delivery task and a risk that recipients miss the later maps. Mina has accepted responsibility for checking the guide's links and approved contact details. The communications team has agreed to label the later delivery clearly. Owen asks the sponsor to approve the staged release rather than describing it as already agreed. He schedules a check-in to review acceptance checks, the map deadline, and remaining risks. The brief combines dependencies, scope choices, ownership, and honest limits, giving the sponsor a concrete recovery decision instead of a vague promise to work faster.
practice.prompt_en: Write 100-140 words presenting the recovery brief. Include the cause of delay, staged option and tradeoff, accepted ownership, approval request, and next check.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫100至140詞的回復計畫摘要，包含延誤原因、分階段方案及代價、已承接責任、核准請求與下次檢查。
practice.sample_answer_en: The welcome pack is late because the approved contact list arrived after the editing slot. The essential guide is drafted, but the optional building maps still need review. I propose releasing the guide first and sending the maps separately. This protects the start date, although it creates another delivery and a risk that recipients miss the maps. Mina has accepted the final checks for working links and approved contact details. Communications will label the later delivery clearly. Please approve this staged release before we announce it. At the next check-in, we will review the acceptance checks, confirm the map deadline, and decide whether any remaining risk requires a change.
